**Golbat** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ゴルバット**_Golbat_) is a dual-type [Poison](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Poison_(type) "Poison (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Zubat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Zubat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Zubat (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 22 and evolves into [Crobat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crobat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Crobat (Pokémon)") when [leveled up with high friendship](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Friendship_Evolution "Friendship Evolution").

(Specifics may differ in past games. Refer to [Game data→Evolution data](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Golbat_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#Evolution_data) for these details.)

## Biology

Golbat is a large, blue, [chiropteran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/bat "wp:bat")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with purple wing membranes. It has small eyes with slit-like pupils, along with tiny triangular ears with purple insides, and a massive mouth with two fangs in each jaw. The fangs are smaller on a female Golbat. While its mouth seems to be otherwise empty, Golbat occasionally displays a long, purple tongue. It has short legs with long, tiny feet. Despite this, Golbat can walk skillfully on the ground.

Golbat's fangs have hollow tubes (similar to straws) specialized for sucking blood. The sharp fangs of Golbat are capable of piercing even the hardest of hides. While they are strong enough to pierce thick hide, they are also unexpectedly fragile. There are some Golbat that have missing fangs as a result of their hunger-fueled attempt to try drinking blood from [Steel-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Steel_(type) "Steel (type)") Pokémon. Golbat feeds on the blood of both Pokémon and humans and is capable of drinking over 10 ounces (300 milliliters) of blood in one sitting. It is gluttonous, and drinks so much blood that its blood type will change to that of its victim following a feed. It occasionally gorges itself to the extent that it becomes too heavy to fly, leaving itself vulnerable in turn. However, it is also willing to share gathered blood with other members of its kind that are hungry. [One particular Golbat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Koga%27s_Golbat "Koga's Golbat") could utilize [Supersonic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Supersonic_(move) "Supersonic (move)") to produce a magic mirror in its mouth for scrying to see things from a distance, even if walls or land are in the way. Golbat is nocturnal and can be found quite easily in [caves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Cave_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat").

### Evolution

Golbat evolves from [Zubat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Zubat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Zubat (Pokémon)") and evolves into [Crobat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crobat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Crobat (Pokémon)").

(For specifics on this Pokémon's Evolution in the games, refer to [Game data→Evolution data](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Golbat_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#Evolution_data).)

**Golbat** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ゴルバット**_Golbat_) is a dual-type [Poison](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Poison_(type) "Poison (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Zubat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Zubat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Zubat (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 22 and evolves into [Crobat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crobat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Crobat (Pokémon)") when [leveled up with high friendship](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Friendship_Evolution "Friendship Evolution").

(Specifics may differ in past games. Refer to [Game data→Evolution data](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Golbat_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#Evolution_data) for these details.)

## Biology

Golbat is a large, blue, [chiropteran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/bat "wp:bat")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with purple wing membranes. It has small eyes with slit-like pupils, along with tiny triangular ears with purple insides, and a massive mouth with two fangs in each jaw. The fangs are smaller on a female Golbat. While its mouth seems to be otherwise empty, Golbat occasionally displays a long, purple tongue. It has short legs with long, tiny feet. Despite this, Golbat can walk skillfully on the ground.

Golbat's fangs have hollow tubes (similar to straws) specialized for sucking blood. The sharp fangs of Golbat are capable of piercing even the hardest of hides. While they are strong enough to pierce thick hide, they are also unexpectedly fragile. There are some Golbat that have missing fangs as a result of their hunger-fueled attempt to try drinking blood from [Steel-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Steel_(type) "Steel (type)") Pokémon. Golbat feeds on the blood of both Pokémon and humans and is capable of drinking over 10 ounces (300 milliliters) of blood in one sitting. It is gluttonous, and drinks so much blood that its blood type will change to that of its victim following a feed. It occasionally gorges itself to the extent that it becomes too heavy to fly, leaving itself vulnerable in turn. However, it is also willing to share gathered blood with other members of its kind that are hungry. [One particular Golbat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Koga%27s_Golbat "Koga's Golbat") could utilize [Supersonic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Supersonic_(move) "Supersonic (move)") to produce a magic mirror in its mouth for scrying to see things from a distance, even if walls or land are in the way. Golbat is nocturnal and can be found quite easily in [caves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Cave_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat").

**Charizard** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **リザードン**_Lizardon_) is a dual-type [Fire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_(type) "Fire (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Charmeleon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmeleon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmeleon (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 36. It is the final form of [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)").

Charizard has three forms:

*   It can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Charizard X** using the [Charizardite X](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_X "Charizardite X") or **Mega Charizard Y** using the [Charizardite Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_Y "Charizardite Y").
*   It can [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") into **Gigantamax Charizard** if it has the [Gigantamax Factor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax#Gigantamax_Factor "Gigantamax").

Charizard is the [game mascot](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Game_mascot "Game mascot") of [Pokémon Red Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), its [international counterpart](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions"), and its [remake](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Remake "Remake"), [Pokémon FireRed Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_FireRed_and_LeafGreen_Versions "Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen Versions"), appearing on the boxart of all three games.

Along with [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)"), [Talonflame](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Talonflame_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Talonflame (Pokémon)"), and [Decidueye](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Decidueye_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Decidueye (Pokémon)"), Charizard is one of the [first Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_the_player%27s_first_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of the player's first Pokémon") available through [Unite licenses](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Unite_license "Unite license") in [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE") as of version 1.12.1.2.

## Biology

Charizard is a [draconic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/dragon "wp:dragon"), bipedal [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)"). It is primarily orange with a cream underside from the chest to the tip of its tail. It has a long neck, small blue eyes, slightly raised nostrils, and two horn-like structures protruding from the back of its rectangular head. Two fangs are visible in its upper jaw when its mouth is closed. Two large wings with blue-green undersides sprout from its back, and a horn-like appendage juts out from the top of the third joint of each wing. A single wing finger is visible through the center of each wing membrane. Charizard's arms are short and skinny compared to its robust belly, and each limb has three white claws. In [Pokémon Red and Green Versions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), Charizard is seemingly shown holding a fireball, implying that it's capable of manipulating its flames using its hands; this is seen in media where it uses [Fire Punch](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_Punch_(move) "Fire Punch (move)"). It has stocky legs with cream-colored soles on each of its [plantigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/plantigrade "wp:plantigrade") feet. The tip of its long, tapering tail burns with a sizable flame, which can intensify to a blue flame if Charizard is irritated.

Charizard flies in search of powerful opponents to battle, and its fire will burn hotter as it gains experience. Its fiery breath can melt boulders and massive glaciers and has been known to cause forest fires accidentally. Though its fiery breath is hot, it never turns it on any opponent weaker than itself. In the [_Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard's Burning Ambitions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP134 "EP134")_, it is established that only a weak Charizard would show off its power. Its wings can carry it to an altitude of 4,600 feet (1,400 meters), but [An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/An_Illustrated_Book_of_POCKET_MONSTERS "An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS") notes that its droppings were found on [Mt. Fuji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt._Fuji "wp:Mt. Fuji"), implying it could fly thrice as high. In the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard Chills](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP105 "EP105")_, it was shown that Charizard is vulnerable to having its tail flame going out in the same way as [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"), as [Ash Ketchum](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") warns [his Charizard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_Charizard "Ash's Charizard") to not let its flame go out. However, the side story episode _[Those Darn Electabuzz!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS17 "HS17")_ showed that Charizard can swim underwater, with [Pokémon Origins](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Origins "Pokémon Origins") further showing that the flame on the tip of the tail can still keep burning underwater. Charizard typically inhabits [mountains and valleys](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Mountain_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"), such as the [Charicific Valley](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charicific_Valley "Charicific Valley") in [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"). However, Charizard can also live in volcanoes, forming packs with other members of its family, including [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"). In [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap"), it's shown that Charizard is fully capable of living inside lava within volcanic craters. In [Pokémon Sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sleep "Pokémon Sleep"), as well as media like the [animated series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_animated_series "Pokémon animated series"), Charizard is known to sleep in an incredibly relaxed position, as it is very confident in its power. A Charizard sleeping flat on its back may be an indicator of that Charizard being especially strong.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-1)

Even though Charizard originally couldn't learn the [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move")[Fly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fly_(move) "Fly (move)"), [Pokémon Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") have been shown riding Charizard in official artwork dating back to the 1997 [Carddass Trading Cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bandai_Pok%C3%A9mon_Carddass_Cards "Bandai Pokémon Carddass Cards"). Ash himself was shown riding his Charizard already in the [second season](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S02 "S02") of the [original series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") of _Pokémon the Series_. Eventually, in [Pokémon Yellow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version "Pokémon Yellow Version"), Charizard became able to learn Fly and has since been frequently depicted as a Pokémon able to carry people on its back to fly them to distant areas. In [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"), Charizard is a [Ride Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ride "Poké Ride") called Charizard Glide, being used by the natives to fly around the region or make deliveries.

### Forms

[![Image 37](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/cd/Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png/250px-Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png)

Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y

Charizard has three alternate forms: [Mega](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") Charizard.

Both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions feature a shorter snout, white, vertical slit pupils, and a bright underside reaching the lower jaw.

[![Image 38](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/89/Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard X from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard X

As Mega Charizard X, its body and legs are more physically fit, though its arms remain thin. Its skin turns black with a sky-blue underside and soles. Two spikes with blue tips curve upward from the front and back of each shoulder, while the tips of its horns sharpen, turn blue, and curve slightly upward. Its brow and claws are larger, and its eyes are now red. It has two small, fin-like spikes under each horn and two more down its lower neck. The finger disappears from the wing membrane, and the lower edges are divided into large, rounded points. The third joint of each wing-arm is adorned with a claw-like spike. It breathes blue flames out the sides of its mouth, and the flame on its tail now burns blue consistently.

The overwhelming power of Mega Evolution causes Mega Charizard X's body to turn black and its intense flames to become blue and burn hotter.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3)

[![Image 39](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/5/59/Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard Y from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard Y

As Mega Charizard Y, it becomes sleeker in appearance but retains its normal coloration. It has three pointed horns on the back of its head, the middle of which is longer. Its snout has larger fangs and a ridge on the nose. Its neck is shorter, but its torso is thinner and longer. It features longer [digitigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/digitigrade "wp:digitigrade") feet. Its hands are less developed, with extremely shortened fingers that are no longer separated from each other. Small wings develop on its wrists, while the ones on its back become larger, lose the wing finger passing through their membrane and end up with ragged edges. The back of its tail has a large spike at the base and three smaller ones near the tip, which now burns with a longer flame.

Mega Charizard Y has an incredible flying prowess that allows it to reach great heights in the sky.[[4]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-4) Its speed and maneuverability is greater than that of a jet fighter,[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3) and the source of its power is said to come from its bond with its [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer").

#### Gigantamax Charizard

[![Image 42](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8a/Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png/220px-Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)

Gigantamax Charizard's wingless body

Gigantamax Charizard's belly is now white instead of its normal cream coloration, with a distinctive pattern of diamonds (some fully colored yellow, others merely outlined in yellow) on the lower portion. A similar pattern (this time filled and edged with a brown color) is on each leg facing forward. Its hand and feet claws are proportionally larger; also, Charizard now stands in a digitigrade stance. The sclerae of the eyes become yellow. The glow of a flame can be seen in the mouth, and the teeth grow, with the lower front teeth and three teeth in the middle now protruding when the mouth is closed. Its tail flame has expanded with respect to its body, growing down the tail towards the body instead of simply sprouting from the end; this enlarged flame is where the three orbiting clouds signature to the Dynamax phenomenon manifest themselves. Each of its horns now emits flames, and its wings have become constructs of pure fire, with burning extensions that outline its clavicle and stop right before they connect on its chest.

Due to being enhanced by Gigantamax energy, the fire within Charizard's body has become much stronger, burning hotter than 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit (2,000 degrees Celsius) and continuing to rise in temperature when Gigantamax Charizard roars. When using its [signature](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move")[G-Max Move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Move "G-Max Move"), [G-Max Wildfire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Wildfire_(move) "G-Max Wildfire (move)"), it launches its colossal fiery wings in the shape of a bird, which circles opponents while continuously scorching them with flames even hotter than magma.[[5]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-5)

This Charizard is always holding a [Charizardite X](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_X "Charizardite X") and will Mega Evolve into Mega Charizard X.
    *   If the player chose [Litten](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Litten_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Litten (Pokémon)"), [Gladion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gladion "Gladion") will have a Charizard in [Title Defense](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Alola)/Title_Defense "Pokémon League (Alola)/Title Defense") a month after completing [Episode RR](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Episode_RR "Episode RR") in [Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ultra_Sun_and_Ultra_Moon "Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon").
    *   [Leon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Leon "Leon")'s signature Pokémon is [his Charizard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Leon%27s_Charizard "Leon's Charizard"), even naming his famous pose after it. Charizard first debuted in [Pokémon Sword and Shield](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sword_and_Shield "Pokémon Sword and Shield") and can [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax").

*   Charizard Glide is a [Poké Ride](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ride "Poké Ride") in [Pokémon Sun and Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sun_and_Moon "Pokémon Sun and Moon") and their sister titles, [Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ultra_Sun_and_Ultra_Moon "Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon").

#### In the side series games

**Charizard** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **リザードン**_Lizardon_) is a dual-type [Fire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_(type) "Fire (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Charmeleon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmeleon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmeleon (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 36. It is the final form of [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)").

Charizard has three forms:

*   It can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Charizard X** using the [Charizardite X](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_X "Charizardite X") or **Mega Charizard Y** using the [Charizardite Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_Y "Charizardite Y").
*   It can [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") into **Gigantamax Charizard** if it has the [Gigantamax Factor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax#Gigantamax_Factor "Gigantamax").

Charizard is the [game mascot](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Game_mascot "Game mascot") of [Pokémon Red Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), its [international counterpart](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions"), and its [remake](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Remake "Remake"), [Pokémon FireRed Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_FireRed_and_LeafGreen_Versions "Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen Versions"), appearing on the boxart of all three games.

Along with [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)"), [Talonflame](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Talonflame_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Talonflame (Pokémon)"), and [Decidueye](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Decidueye_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Decidueye (Pokémon)"), Charizard is one of the [first Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_the_player%27s_first_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of the player's first Pokémon") available through [Unite licenses](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Unite_license "Unite license") in [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE") as of version 1.12.1.2.

## Biology

Charizard is a [draconic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/dragon "wp:dragon"), bipedal [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)"). It is primarily orange with a cream underside from the chest to the tip of its tail. It has a long neck, small blue eyes, slightly raised nostrils, and two horn-like structures protruding from the back of its rectangular head. Two fangs are visible in its upper jaw when its mouth is closed. Two large wings with blue-green undersides sprout from its back, and a horn-like appendage juts out from the top of the third joint of each wing. A single wing finger is visible through the center of each wing membrane. Charizard's arms are short and skinny compared to its robust belly, and each limb has three white claws. In [Pokémon Red and Green Versions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), Charizard is seemingly shown holding a fireball, implying that it's capable of manipulating its flames using its hands; this is seen in media where it uses [Fire Punch](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_Punch_(move) "Fire Punch (move)"). It has stocky legs with cream-colored soles on each of its [plantigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/plantigrade "wp:plantigrade") feet. The tip of its long, tapering tail burns with a sizable flame, which can intensify to a blue flame if Charizard is irritated.

Charizard flies in search of powerful opponents to battle, and its fire will burn hotter as it gains experience. Its fiery breath can melt boulders and massive glaciers and has been known to cause forest fires accidentally. Though its fiery breath is hot, it never turns it on any opponent weaker than itself. In the [_Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard's Burning Ambitions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP134 "EP134")_, it is established that only a weak Charizard would show off its power. Its wings can carry it to an altitude of 4,600 feet (1,400 meters), but [An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/An_Illustrated_Book_of_POCKET_MONSTERS "An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS") notes that its droppings were found on [Mt. Fuji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt._Fuji "wp:Mt. Fuji"), implying it could fly thrice as high. In the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard Chills](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP105 "EP105")_, it was shown that Charizard is vulnerable to having its tail flame going out in the same way as [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"), as [Ash Ketchum](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") warns [his Charizard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_Charizard "Ash's Charizard") to not let its flame go out. However, the side story episode _[Those Darn Electabuzz!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS17 "HS17")_ showed that Charizard can swim underwater, with [Pokémon Origins](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Origins "Pokémon Origins") further showing that the flame on the tip of the tail can still keep burning underwater. Charizard typically inhabits [mountains and valleys](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Mountain_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"), such as the [Charicific Valley](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charicific_Valley "Charicific Valley") in [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"). However, Charizard can also live in volcanoes, forming packs with other members of its family, including [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"). In [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap"), it's shown that Charizard is fully capable of living inside lava within volcanic craters. In [Pokémon Sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sleep "Pokémon Sleep"), as well as media like the [animated series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_animated_series "Pokémon animated series"), Charizard is known to sleep in an incredibly relaxed position, as it is very confident in its power. A Charizard sleeping flat on its back may be an indicator of that Charizard being especially strong.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-1)

Even though Charizard originally couldn't learn the [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move")[Fly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fly_(move) "Fly (move)"), [Pokémon Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") have been shown riding Charizard in official artwork dating back to the 1997 [Carddass Trading Cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bandai_Pok%C3%A9mon_Carddass_Cards "Bandai Pokémon Carddass Cards"). Ash himself was shown riding his Charizard already in the [second season](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S02 "S02") of the [original series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") of _Pokémon the Series_. Eventually, in [Pokémon Yellow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version "Pokémon Yellow Version"), Charizard became able to learn Fly and has since been frequently depicted as a Pokémon able to carry people on its back to fly them to distant areas. In [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"), Charizard is a [Ride Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ride "Poké Ride") called Charizard Glide, being used by the natives to fly around the region or make deliveries.

Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y

Charizard has three alternate forms: [Mega](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") Charizard.

Both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions feature a shorter snout, white, vertical slit pupils, and a bright underside reaching the lower jaw.

#### Mega Charizard X

As Mega Charizard X, its body and legs are more physically fit, though its arms remain thin. Its skin turns black with a sky-blue underside and soles. Two spikes with blue tips curve upward from the front and back of each shoulder, while the tips of its horns sharpen, turn blue, and curve slightly upward. Its brow and claws are larger, and its eyes are now red. It has two small, fin-like spikes under each horn and two more down its lower neck. The finger disappears from the wing membrane, and the lower edges are divided into large, rounded points. The third joint of each wing-arm is adorned with a claw-like spike. It breathes blue flames out the sides of its mouth, and the flame on its tail now burns blue consistently.

The overwhelming power of Mega Evolution causes Mega Charizard X's body to turn black and its intense flames to become blue and burn hotter.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard Y from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard Y

As Mega Charizard Y, it becomes sleeker in appearance but retains its normal coloration. It has three pointed horns on the back of its head, the middle of which is longer. Its snout has larger fangs and a ridge on the nose. Its neck is shorter, but its torso is thinner and longer. It features longer [digitigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/digitigrade "wp:digitigrade") feet. Its hands are less developed, with extremely shortened fingers that are no longer separated from each other. Small wings develop on its wrists, while the ones on its back become larger, lose the wing finger passing through their membrane and end up with ragged edges. The back of its tail has a large spike at the base and three smaller ones near the tip, which now burns with a longer flame.

Mega Charizard Y has an incredible flying prowess that allows it to reach great heights in the sky.[[4]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-4) Its speed and maneuverability is greater than that of a jet fighter,[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3) and the source of its power is said to come from its bond with its [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer").

#### Gigantamax Charizard

[![Image 42](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8a/Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png/220px-Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)

Gigantamax Charizard's wingless body

Gigantamax Charizard's belly is now white instead of its normal cream coloration, with a distinctive pattern of diamonds (some fully colored yellow, others merely outlined in yellow) on the lower portion. A similar pattern (this time filled and edged with a brown color) is on each leg facing forward. Its hand and feet claws are proportionally larger; also, Charizard now stands in a digitigrade stance. The sclerae of the eyes become yellow. The glow of a flame can be seen in the mouth, and the teeth grow, with the lower front teeth and three teeth in the middle now protruding when the mouth is closed. Its tail flame has expanded with respect to its body, growing down the tail towards the body instead of simply sprouting from the end; this enlarged flame is where the three orbiting clouds signature to the Dynamax phenomenon manifest themselves. Each of its horns now emits flames, and its wings have become constructs of pure fire, with burning extensions that outline its clavicle and stop right before they connect on its chest.

Due to being enhanced by Gigantamax energy, the fire within Charizard's body has become much stronger, burning hotter than 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit (2,000 degrees Celsius) and continuing to rise in temperature when Gigantamax Charizard roars. When using its [signature](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move")[G-Max Move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Move "G-Max Move"), [G-Max Wildfire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Wildfire_(move) "G-Max Wildfire (move)"), it launches its colossal fiery wings in the shape of a bird, which circles opponents while continuously scorching them with flames even hotter than magma.[[5]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Charizard_X#cite_note-5)

**Charizard** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **リザードン**_Lizardon_) is a dual-type [Fire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_(type) "Fire (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Charmeleon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmeleon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmeleon (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 36. It is the final form of [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)").

Charizard has three forms:

*   It can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Charizard X** using the [Charizardite X](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_X "Charizardite X") or **Mega Charizard Y** using the [Charizardite Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_Y "Charizardite Y").
*   It can [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") into **Gigantamax Charizard** if it has the [Gigantamax Factor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax#Gigantamax_Factor "Gigantamax").

Charizard is the [game mascot](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Game_mascot "Game mascot") of [Pokémon Red Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), its [international counterpart](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions"), and its [remake](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Remake "Remake"), [Pokémon FireRed Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_FireRed_and_LeafGreen_Versions "Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen Versions"), appearing on the boxart of all three games.

Along with [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)"), [Talonflame](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Talonflame_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Talonflame (Pokémon)"), and [Decidueye](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Decidueye_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Decidueye (Pokémon)"), Charizard is one of the [first Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_the_player%27s_first_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of the player's first Pokémon") available through [Unite licenses](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Unite_license "Unite license") in [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE") as of version 1.12.1.2.

## Biology

Charizard is a [draconic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/dragon "wp:dragon"), bipedal [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)"). It is primarily orange with a cream underside from the chest to the tip of its tail. It has a long neck, small blue eyes, slightly raised nostrils, and two horn-like structures protruding from the back of its rectangular head. Two fangs are visible in its upper jaw when its mouth is closed. Two large wings with blue-green undersides sprout from its back, and a horn-like appendage juts out from the top of the third joint of each wing. A single wing finger is visible through the center of each wing membrane. Charizard's arms are short and skinny compared to its robust belly, and each limb has three white claws. In [Pokémon Red and Green Versions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), Charizard is seemingly shown holding a fireball, implying that it's capable of manipulating its flames using its hands; this is seen in media where it uses [Fire Punch](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_Punch_(move) "Fire Punch (move)"). It has stocky legs with cream-colored soles on each of its [plantigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/plantigrade "wp:plantigrade") feet. The tip of its long, tapering tail burns with a sizable flame, which can intensify to a blue flame if Charizard is irritated.

Charizard flies in search of powerful opponents to battle, and its fire will burn hotter as it gains experience. Its fiery breath can melt boulders and massive glaciers and has been known to cause forest fires accidentally. Though its fiery breath is hot, it never turns it on any opponent weaker than itself. In the [_Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard's Burning Ambitions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP134 "EP134")_, it is established that only a weak Charizard would show off its power. Its wings can carry it to an altitude of 4,600 feet (1,400 meters), but [An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/An_Illustrated_Book_of_POCKET_MONSTERS "An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS") notes that its droppings were found on [Mt. Fuji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt._Fuji "wp:Mt. Fuji"), implying it could fly thrice as high. In the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard Chills](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP105 "EP105")_, it was shown that Charizard is vulnerable to having its tail flame going out in the same way as [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"), as [Ash Ketchum](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") warns [his Charizard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_Charizard "Ash's Charizard") to not let its flame go out. However, the side story episode _[Those Darn Electabuzz!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS17 "HS17")_ showed that Charizard can swim underwater, with [Pokémon Origins](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Origins "Pokémon Origins") further showing that the flame on the tip of the tail can still keep burning underwater. Charizard typically inhabits [mountains and valleys](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Mountain_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"), such as the [Charicific Valley](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charicific_Valley "Charicific Valley") in [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"). However, Charizard can also live in volcanoes, forming packs with other members of its family, including [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"). In [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap"), it's shown that Charizard is fully capable of living inside lava within volcanic craters. In [Pokémon Sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sleep "Pokémon Sleep"), as well as media like the [animated series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_animated_series "Pokémon animated series"), Charizard is known to sleep in an incredibly relaxed position, as it is very confident in its power. A Charizard sleeping flat on its back may be an indicator of that Charizard being especially strong.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1)

Even though Charizard originally couldn't learn the [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move")[Fly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fly_(move) "Fly (move)"), [Pokémon Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") have been shown riding Charizard in official artwork dating back to the 1997 [Carddass Trading Cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bandai_Pok%C3%A9mon_Carddass_Cards "Bandai Pokémon Carddass Cards"). Ash himself was shown riding his Charizard already in the [second season](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S02 "S02") of the [original series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") of _Pokémon the Series_. Eventually, in [Pokémon Yellow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version "Pokémon Yellow Version"), Charizard became able to learn Fly and has since been frequently depicted as a Pokémon able to carry people on its back to fly them to distant areas. In [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"), Charizard is a [Ride Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ride "Poké Ride") called Charizard Glide, being used by the natives to fly around the region or make deliveries.

### Forms

[![Image 37](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/cd/Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png/250px-Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png)

Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y

Charizard has three alternate forms: [Mega](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") Charizard.

Both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions feature a shorter snout, white, vertical slit pupils, and a bright underside reaching the lower jaw.

[![Image 38](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/89/Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard X from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard X

As Mega Charizard X, its body and legs are more physically fit, though its arms remain thin. Its skin turns black with a sky-blue underside and soles. Two spikes with blue tips curve upward from the front and back of each shoulder, while the tips of its horns sharpen, turn blue, and curve slightly upward. Its brow and claws are larger, and its eyes are now red. It has two small, fin-like spikes under each horn and two more down its lower neck. The finger disappears from the wing membrane, and the lower edges are divided into large, rounded points. The third joint of each wing-arm is adorned with a claw-like spike. It breathes blue flames out the sides of its mouth, and the flame on its tail now burns blue consistently.

The overwhelming power of Mega Evolution causes Mega Charizard X's body to turn black and its intense flames to become blue and burn hotter.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3)

[![Image 39](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/5/59/Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard Y from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard Y

As Mega Charizard Y, it becomes sleeker in appearance but retains its normal coloration. It has three pointed horns on the back of its head, the middle of which is longer. Its snout has larger fangs and a ridge on the nose. Its neck is shorter, but its torso is thinner and longer. It features longer [digitigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/digitigrade "wp:digitigrade") feet. Its hands are less developed, with extremely shortened fingers that are no longer separated from each other. Small wings develop on its wrists, while the ones on its back become larger, lose the wing finger passing through their membrane and end up with ragged edges. The back of its tail has a large spike at the base and three smaller ones near the tip, which now burns with a longer flame.

Mega Charizard Y has an incredible flying prowess that allows it to reach great heights in the sky.[[4]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-4) Its speed and maneuverability is greater than that of a jet fighter,[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3) and the source of its power is said to come from its bond with its [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer").

#### Gigantamax Charizard

[![Image 42](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8a/Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png/220px-Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)

Gigantamax Charizard's wingless body

Gigantamax Charizard's belly is now white instead of its normal cream coloration, with a distinctive pattern of diamonds (some fully colored yellow, others merely outlined in yellow) on the lower portion. A similar pattern (this time filled and edged with a brown color) is on each leg facing forward. Its hand and feet claws are proportionally larger; also, Charizard now stands in a digitigrade stance. The sclerae of the eyes become yellow. The glow of a flame can be seen in the mouth, and the teeth grow, with the lower front teeth and three teeth in the middle now protruding when the mouth is closed. Its tail flame has expanded with respect to its body, growing down the tail towards the body instead of simply sprouting from the end; this enlarged flame is where the three orbiting clouds signature to the Dynamax phenomenon manifest themselves. Each of its horns now emits flames, and its wings have become constructs of pure fire, with burning extensions that outline its clavicle and stop right before they connect on its chest.

Due to being enhanced by Gigantamax energy, the fire within Charizard's body has become much stronger, burning hotter than 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit (2,000 degrees Celsius) and continuing to rise in temperature when Gigantamax Charizard roars. When using its [signature](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move")[G-Max Move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Move "G-Max Move"), [G-Max Wildfire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Wildfire_(move) "G-Max Wildfire (move)"), it launches its colossal fiery wings in the shape of a bird, which circles opponents while continuously scorching them with flames even hotter than magma.[[5]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-5)

### Evolution

Charizard [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Charmeleon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmeleon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmeleon (Pokémon)") and is the final form of [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)").

**Charizard** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **リザードン**_Lizardon_) is a dual-type [Fire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_(type) "Fire (type)")/[Flying](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Flying_(type) "Flying (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_I "Generation I").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Charmeleon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmeleon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmeleon (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 36. It is the final form of [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)").

Charizard has three forms:

*   It can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Charizard X** using the [Charizardite X](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_X "Charizardite X") or **Mega Charizard Y** using the [Charizardite Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizardite_Y "Charizardite Y").
*   It can [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") into **Gigantamax Charizard** if it has the [Gigantamax Factor](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax#Gigantamax_Factor "Gigantamax").

Charizard is the [game mascot](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Game_mascot "Game mascot") of [Pokémon Red Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), its [international counterpart](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions"), and its [remake](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Remake "Remake"), [Pokémon FireRed Version](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_FireRed_and_LeafGreen_Versions "Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen Versions"), appearing on the boxart of all three games.

Along with [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)"), [Talonflame](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Talonflame_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Talonflame (Pokémon)"), and [Decidueye](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Decidueye_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Decidueye (Pokémon)"), Charizard is one of the [first Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_the_player%27s_first_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of the player's first Pokémon") available through [Unite licenses](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Unite_license "Unite license") in [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE") as of version 1.12.1.2.

## Biology

Charizard is a [draconic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/dragon "wp:dragon"), bipedal [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)"). It is primarily orange with a cream underside from the chest to the tip of its tail. It has a long neck, small blue eyes, slightly raised nostrils, and two horn-like structures protruding from the back of its rectangular head. Two fangs are visible in its upper jaw when its mouth is closed. Two large wings with blue-green undersides sprout from its back, and a horn-like appendage juts out from the top of the third joint of each wing. A single wing finger is visible through the center of each wing membrane. Charizard's arms are short and skinny compared to its robust belly, and each limb has three white claws. In [Pokémon Red and Green Versions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Green_Versions "Pokémon Red and Green Versions"), Charizard is seemingly shown holding a fireball, implying that it's capable of manipulating its flames using its hands; this is seen in media where it uses [Fire Punch](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_Punch_(move) "Fire Punch (move)"). It has stocky legs with cream-colored soles on each of its [plantigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/plantigrade "wp:plantigrade") feet. The tip of its long, tapering tail burns with a sizable flame, which can intensify to a blue flame if Charizard is irritated.

Charizard flies in search of powerful opponents to battle, and its fire will burn hotter as it gains experience. Its fiery breath can melt boulders and massive glaciers and has been known to cause forest fires accidentally. Though its fiery breath is hot, it never turns it on any opponent weaker than itself. In the [_Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard's Burning Ambitions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP134 "EP134")_, it is established that only a weak Charizard would show off its power. Its wings can carry it to an altitude of 4,600 feet (1,400 meters), but [An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/An_Illustrated_Book_of_POCKET_MONSTERS "An Illustrated Book of POCKET MONSTERS") notes that its droppings were found on [Mt. Fuji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt._Fuji "wp:Mt. Fuji"), implying it could fly thrice as high. In the [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") episode _[Charizard Chills](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/EP105 "EP105")_, it was shown that Charizard is vulnerable to having its tail flame going out in the same way as [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"), as [Ash Ketchum](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") warns [his Charizard](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash%27s_Charizard "Ash's Charizard") to not let its flame go out. However, the side story episode _[Those Darn Electabuzz!](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/HS17 "HS17")_ showed that Charizard can swim underwater, with [Pokémon Origins](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Origins "Pokémon Origins") further showing that the flame on the tip of the tail can still keep burning underwater. Charizard typically inhabits [mountains and valleys](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Mountain_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat"), such as the [Charicific Valley](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charicific_Valley "Charicific Valley") in [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"). However, Charizard can also live in volcanoes, forming packs with other members of its family, including [Charmander](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charmander_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Charmander (Pokémon)"). In [Pokémon Snap](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Snap "Pokémon Snap"), it's shown that Charizard is fully capable of living inside lava within volcanic craters. In [Pokémon Sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sleep "Pokémon Sleep"), as well as media like the [animated series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_animated_series "Pokémon animated series"), Charizard is known to sleep in an incredibly relaxed position, as it is very confident in its power. A Charizard sleeping flat on its back may be an indicator of that Charizard being especially strong.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1)

Even though Charizard originally couldn't learn the [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move")[Fly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fly_(move) "Fly (move)"), [Pokémon Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") have been shown riding Charizard in official artwork dating back to the 1997 [Carddass Trading Cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bandai_Pok%C3%A9mon_Carddass_Cards "Bandai Pokémon Carddass Cards"). Ash himself was shown riding his Charizard already in the [second season](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/S02 "S02") of the [original series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series") of _Pokémon the Series_. Eventually, in [Pokémon Yellow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version "Pokémon Yellow Version"), Charizard became able to learn Fly and has since been frequently depicted as a Pokémon able to carry people on its back to fly them to distant areas. In [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"), Charizard is a [Ride Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ride "Poké Ride") called Charizard Glide, being used by the natives to fly around the region or make deliveries.

### Forms

[![Image 37](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/c/cd/Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png/250px-Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_X_Mega_Charizard_Y_artwork_2.png)

Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y

Charizard has three alternate forms: [Mega](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and [Gigantamax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gigantamax "Gigantamax") Charizard.

Both of Charizard's Mega Evolutions feature a shorter snout, white, vertical slit pupils, and a bright underside reaching the lower jaw.

[![Image 38](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/89/Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_X_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard X from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard X

As Mega Charizard X, its body and legs are more physically fit, though its arms remain thin. Its skin turns black with a sky-blue underside and soles. Two spikes with blue tips curve upward from the front and back of each shoulder, while the tips of its horns sharpen, turn blue, and curve slightly upward. Its brow and claws are larger, and its eyes are now red. It has two small, fin-like spikes under each horn and two more down its lower neck. The finger disappears from the wing membrane, and the lower edges are divided into large, rounded points. The third joint of each wing-arm is adorned with a claw-like spike. It breathes blue flames out the sides of its mouth, and the flame on its tail now burns blue consistently.

The overwhelming power of Mega Evolution causes Mega Charizard X's body to turn black and its intense flames to become blue and burn hotter.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3)

[![Image 39](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/5/59/Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Charizard_Y_XY_concept_art.jpg)

Concept art featuring Mega Charizard Y from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

#### Mega Charizard Y

As Mega Charizard Y, it becomes sleeker in appearance but retains its normal coloration. It has three pointed horns on the back of its head, the middle of which is longer. Its snout has larger fangs and a ridge on the nose. Its neck is shorter, but its torso is thinner and longer. It features longer [digitigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/digitigrade "wp:digitigrade") feet. Its hands are less developed, with extremely shortened fingers that are no longer separated from each other. Small wings develop on its wrists, while the ones on its back become larger, lose the wing finger passing through their membrane and end up with ragged edges. The back of its tail has a large spike at the base and three smaller ones near the tip, which now burns with a longer flame.

Mega Charizard Y has an incredible flying prowess that allows it to reach great heights in the sky.[[4]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-4) Its speed and maneuverability is greater than that of a jet fighter,[[3]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-MEgaCharizardXY-3) and the source of its power is said to come from its bond with its [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer").

#### Gigantamax Charizard

[![Image 42](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8a/Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png/220px-Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Leon_Charizard_G-Max_Wildfire.png)

Gigantamax Charizard's wingless body

Gigantamax Charizard's belly is now white instead of its normal cream coloration, with a distinctive pattern of diamonds (some fully colored yellow, others merely outlined in yellow) on the lower portion. A similar pattern (this time filled and edged with a brown color) is on each leg facing forward. Its hand and feet claws are proportionally larger; also, Charizard now stands in a digitigrade stance. The sclerae of the eyes become yellow. The glow of a flame can be seen in the mouth, and the teeth grow, with the lower front teeth and three teeth in the middle now protruding when the mouth is closed. Its tail flame has expanded with respect to its body, growing down the tail towards the body instead of simply sprouting from the end; this enlarged flame is where the three orbiting clouds signature to the Dynamax phenomenon manifest themselves. Each of its horns now emits flames, and its wings have become constructs of pure fire, with burning extensions that outline its clavicle and stop right before they connect on its chest.

Due to being enhanced by Gigantamax energy, the fire within Charizard's body has become much stronger, burning hotter than 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit (2,000 degrees Celsius) and continuing to rise in temperature when Gigantamax Charizard roars. When using its [signature](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move")[G-Max Move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Move "G-Max Move"), [G-Max Wildfire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/G-Max_Wildfire_(move) "G-Max Wildfire (move)"), it launches its colossal fiery wings in the shape of a bird, which circles opponents while continuously scorching them with flames even hotter than magma.[[5]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Charizard_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-5)

Logo

These Pokémon were distributed at the Pokémon Center New York Gotta catch 'em all! Station.

Players could obtain one Pokémon while the machine was running and not to exceed one Pokémon per day in the event the machine was restarted.

The Pokémon in a distribution have a 15% total chance of being Shiny unless otherwise specified. All Pokémon except evolved, Legendary and Mythical Pokémon are distributed as Eggs.

**Gardevoir** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **サーナイト**_Sirnight_) is a dual-type [Psychic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(type) "Psychic (type)")/[Fairy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fairy_(type) "Fairy (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation III](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_III "Generation III"). Prior to [Generation VI](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VI "Generation VI"), it was a pure [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(type) "Psychic (type)") Pokémon.

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Kirlia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kirlia_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Kirlia (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 30. It is one of [Ralts](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ralts_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Ralts (Pokémon)")'s final forms, the other being [Gallade](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Gallade (Pokémon)").

Gardevoir can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Gardevoir** using the [Gardevoirite](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gardevoirite "Gardevoirite").

The [Paradox Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paradox_Pok%C3%A9mon "Paradox Pokémon")[Iron Valiant](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Iron_Valiant_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Iron Valiant (Pokémon)") is said to be a future relative of Gardevoir and Gallade or a version of them from a parallel timeline.

## Biology

Gardevoir is a bipedal, humanoid [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") whose body resembles a flowing gown. Most of its body is white, but its hair, arms, and the underside of its gown are green. Its hair curls over its face and down the sides of its head. Behind its red eyes are short spikes, resembling a masquerade mask. It has long arms with three fingers on each hand and slender white legs. A red, fin-like plate goes through its chest and extends from the back. A band of green on its chest extends to the center of the plate's front half and connects to its sleeve-like arms.

Gardevoir is able to see the future using its psychic powers. Its telekinetic powers enable it to lift objects and support itself without feeling the pull of gravity. Additionally, it is able to create small black holes, distort dimensions, and fire [a destructive energy wave](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Aura_Sphere_(move) "Aura Sphere (move)"). Gardevoir's power reaches its peak when protecting its [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer"), whom it will protect with its life. This Pokémon typically inhabits [urban areas](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Urban_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat") and snowy regions. As mentioned in [Pokémon Sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sleep "Pokémon Sleep"), Gardevoir often sleeps upright in order to protect people or Pokémon instantly at any moment.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gardevoir_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1) There is a rumor that if anyone sees Gardevoir moving its dress-like body in its sleep, they will never forget that beautiful sight.

[Iron Valiant](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Iron_Valiant_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Iron Valiant (Pokémon)") shares a resemblance to both Gardevoir and [Gallade](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Gallade (Pokémon)"). Iron Valiant is theorized to be in fact a robot, the product of a mad scientist’s efforts to create the most powerful psychic Pokémon of all. According to [AI Turo](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AI_Turo "AI Turo"), the Pokémon is a descendent of Gardevoir and Gallade from the distant future. However, according to a version of [Professor Turo](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Professor_Turo "Professor Turo") that was summoned at the [Crystal Pool](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crystal_Pool "Crystal Pool"), it is a counterpart of Gardevoir and Gallade from a [parallel timeline](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_multiverse "Pokémon multiverse").

### Forms

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/9/91/Mega_Gardevoir_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Gardevoir_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Gardevoir_XY_concept_art.jpg)

[Concept art](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Concept_art_from_Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "a:Category:Concept art from Pokémon X and Y") featuring Mega Gardevoir from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

Gardevoir can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into Mega Gardevoir.

As Mega Gardevoir, it turns almost completely white; only its hair remains green. Its gown becomes longer and wider, resembling a bridal gown. The forearms are slightly thicker with a pointed extension above the elbow, resembling gloves. Its facial spikes are larger and now curl upwards. In contrast, its hair is now shorter and more tightly curled. The plate in its chest has now split in two in the front, the halves extending to either side. The plate is said to be a physical manifestation of this Pokémon's heart, and it is able to use tremendous psychic power now that it is open.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gardevoir_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-2)

Gardevoir evolves from [Kirlia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kirlia_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Kirlia (Pokémon)") and is one of the final forms of [Ralts](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ralts_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Ralts (Pokémon)"), the other being [Gallade](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Gallade (Pokémon)").

**Gardevoir** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **サーナイト**_Sirnight_) is a dual-type [Psychic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(type) "Psychic (type)")/[Fairy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fairy_(type) "Fairy (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation III](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_III "Generation III"). Prior to [Generation VI](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VI "Generation VI"), it was a pure [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(type) "Psychic (type)") Pokémon.

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Kirlia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kirlia_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Kirlia (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 30. It is one of [Ralts](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ralts_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Ralts (Pokémon)")'s final forms, the other being [Gallade](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Gallade (Pokémon)").

Gardevoir can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into **Mega Gardevoir** using the [Gardevoirite](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gardevoirite "Gardevoirite").

The [Paradox Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paradox_Pok%C3%A9mon "Paradox Pokémon")[Iron Valiant](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Iron_Valiant_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Iron Valiant (Pokémon)") is said to be a future relative of Gardevoir and Gallade or a version of them from a parallel timeline.

## Biology

Gardevoir is a bipedal, humanoid [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") whose body resembles a flowing gown. Most of its body is white, but its hair, arms, and the underside of its gown are green. Its hair curls over its face and down the sides of its head. Behind its red eyes are short spikes, resembling a masquerade mask. It has long arms with three fingers on each hand and slender white legs. A red, fin-like plate goes through its chest and extends from the back. A band of green on its chest extends to the center of the plate's front half and connects to its sleeve-like arms.

Gardevoir is able to see the future using its psychic powers. Its telekinetic powers enable it to lift objects and support itself without feeling the pull of gravity. Additionally, it is able to create small black holes, distort dimensions, and fire [a destructive energy wave](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Aura_Sphere_(move) "Aura Sphere (move)"). Gardevoir's power reaches its peak when protecting its [Trainer](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer"), whom it will protect with its life. This Pokémon typically inhabits [urban areas](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_habitat#Urban_Pok%C3%A9mon "List of Pokémon by habitat") and snowy regions. As mentioned in [Pokémon Sleep](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sleep "Pokémon Sleep"), Gardevoir often sleeps upright in order to protect people or Pokémon instantly at any moment.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gardevoir_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1) There is a rumor that if anyone sees Gardevoir moving its dress-like body in its sleep, they will never forget that beautiful sight.

[Iron Valiant](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Iron_Valiant_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Iron Valiant (Pokémon)") shares a resemblance to both Gardevoir and [Gallade](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gallade_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Gallade (Pokémon)"). Iron Valiant is theorized to be in fact a robot, the product of a mad scientist’s efforts to create the most powerful psychic Pokémon of all. According to [AI Turo](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/AI_Turo "AI Turo"), the Pokémon is a descendent of Gardevoir and Gallade from the distant future. However, according to a version of [Professor Turo](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Professor_Turo "Professor Turo") that was summoned at the [Crystal Pool](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crystal_Pool "Crystal Pool"), it is a counterpart of Gardevoir and Gallade from a [parallel timeline](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_multiverse "Pokémon multiverse").

### Forms

[![Image 32](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/9/91/Mega_Gardevoir_XY_concept_art.jpg/250px-Mega_Gardevoir_XY_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Mega_Gardevoir_XY_concept_art.jpg)

[Concept art](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Concept_art_from_Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "a:Category:Concept art from Pokémon X and Y") featuring Mega Gardevoir from [Pokémon X and Y](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y "Pokémon X and Y")

Gardevoir can [Mega Evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mega_Evolution "Mega Evolution") into Mega Gardevoir.

As Mega Gardevoir, it turns almost completely white; only its hair remains green. Its gown becomes longer and wider, resembling a bridal gown. The forearms are slightly thicker with a pointed extension above the elbow, resembling gloves. Its facial spikes are larger and now curl upwards. In contrast, its hair is now shorter and more tightly curled. The plate in its chest has now split in two in the front, the halves extending to either side. The plate is said to be a physical manifestation of this Pokémon's heart, and it is able to use tremendous psychic power now that it is open.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gardevoir_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-2)
