The **Pokémon World Championships** (Japanese: **ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス**_Pokémon World Championships_), often referred to as simply **Worlds** or abbreviated as **WCS** are an annual event held by the [Play! Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Play!_Pok%C3%A9mon "Play! Pokémon") organized play division of [The Pokémon Company International](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/The_Pok%C3%A9mon_Company_International "The Pokémon Company International"). They function as the finals for both the [Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") and [Video Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Core_series "Core series") Championships. Since 2015, the World Championships have also featured events for [spin-off Pokémon games](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Spin-off_Pok%C3%A9mon_games "Spin-off Pokémon games"), namely [Pokkén Tournament](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pokk%C3%A9n_Tournament "Pokkén Tournament"), [Pokémon GO](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO "Pokémon GO"), and [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE"). The Pokémon World Championships are held annually, occurring every August.

Competitors usually must qualify for the event based on their performance in other events in the same season, such as regional championships, national championships, dedicated qualifying tournaments, or the previous year's World Championships. The exact qualification requirements depend on the year, the region the player is from, and the game in which they are playing.

While the Pokémon World Championships are held as a single unified event featuring multiple different games, each of the games are run as an entirely separate tournament. Competitors compete in only one of the featured games, and the qualification requirements of each are entirely separate. Additionally, competitors usually are separated into one of three age groups, meaning that three world champions are crowned for each game each year.

Minor announcements are usually made during the events, such as upcoming VGC mechanics and variants of TCG cards, teasers for the ruleset of the following VGC format, and the city where the next World Championships will be hosted.

## History

### Predecessors

Before the introduction of the modern Pokémon World Championships, both the TCG and video games held some international competitions.

For the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the [Pokémon Tropical Mega Battle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Tropical_Mega_Battle "Pokémon Tropical Mega Battle") was an international Pokémon Trading Card Game tournament held annually from 1999 to 2002 in Hawaii by [Wizards of the Coast](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wizards_of_the_Coast "Wizards of the Coast"), the distributor of the Pokémon Trading Card Game in many regions outside of Japan at the time. Players from Canada, Latin America, Europe, the United States, and Japan were invited to the event.

In September 2000, to coincide with the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "wp:2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, Australia, the [first ever Pokémon World Championship](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/w/index.php?title=2000_World_Championships&action=edit&redlink=1 "2000 World Championships (page does not exist)") was also held in Sydney. Players from Australia, Belgium, [France](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_France "Pokémon in France"), [Germany](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_Germany "Pokémon in Germany"), [the Netherlands](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_the_Netherlands "Pokémon in the Netherlands"), [Spain](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_Spain "Pokémon in Spain"), [the United Kingdom](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_the_United_Kingdom "Pokémon in the United Kingdom"), and [the United States](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_the_United_States "Pokémon in the United States") competed using [Pokémon Red and Blue](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions") and [Pokémon Yellow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version "Pokémon Yellow Version"). This was a one-time event, with a video game World Championship not being held again until 2009.

### Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships

In August 2002, Wizards of the Coast held the [first Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championship](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2002_World_Championships_(TCG) "2002 World Championships (TCG)") in Seattle, Washington in the United States.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-1)

Due to Wizards of the Coast's license to distribute the Pokémon Trading Card Game reverting to The Pokémon Company in 2003, no World Championship was held that year. Now with control of the Pokémon Trading Card Game licence, [Pokémon USA](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_USA "Pokémon USA") formed [Pokémon Organized Play](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Organized_Play "Pokémon Organized Play") to manage Pokémon Trading Card Game events.

In August 2004, Pokémon Organized Play held the [2004 Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2004_World_Championships_(TCG) "2004 World Championships (TCG)"). From 2004 to 2008, the event was titled the Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships, reflecting the fact that it was specifically for the Pokémon Trading Card Game only.

At the [2008 Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2008_World_Championships_(TCG) "2008 World Championships (TCG)"), a special video game event called the [Pokémon Video Game Showdown 2008](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Video_Game_Showdown_2008 "Pokémon Video Game Showdown 2008") was held. This event featured players from the United States and Japan competing with [Pokémon Diamond and Pearl](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Diamond_and_Pearl_Versions "Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Versions"). However, since only two countries were involved, the winner was not awarded the title of world champion.

### Pokémon World Championships

In August 2009, the first unified Pokémon World Championships were held, featuring both the Pokémon Trading Card Game and the Pokémon Video Game Championships. This has been the structure used for the Pokémon World Championships ever since.

From 2015 to 2022, [Pokkén Tournament](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pokk%C3%A9n_Tournament "Pokkén Tournament") was also featured at the Pokémon World Championships. In 2015, the Pokkén Tournament competition was run as an invitational due to the lack of preliminary events. After the 2022 World Championships, it was announced that Pokkén Tournament would no longer appear at the Pokémon World Championships.

Starting in 2019, [Pokémon GO](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO "Pokémon GO") was added to the Pokémon World Championships. In 2019, the Pokémon GO competition was run as an invitational due to the lack of preliminary events.

Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the planned 2020 Pokémon World Championships to be held in London, England were cancelled, and the event also was not held in 2021. The World Championships returned with the [2022 Pokémon World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2022_World_Championships "2022 World Championships"), held in London, England like the original 2020 plan.

From 2022 to 2026, [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE") was featured the Pokémon World Championships. Beginning with the 2027 competitive season, UNITE's championship tournament will instead be held at a separate event, the [Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE_Aeos_Crown_2027_Tokyo&action=edit&redlink=1 "Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo (page does not exist)").

## Video Game Championship

The [core series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Core_series "Core series") Pokémon games were first featured at a Nintendo-organized World Championship event in 2000 with single battles, and later returning as [Pokémon Video Game Showdown](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Video_Game_Showdown "Pokémon Video Game Showdown") (VGS) in 2008 as a side-event to the [2008 Trading Card Game World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2008_World_Championships_(TCG) "2008 World Championships (TCG)") with double battles. Starting in 2009, the events were renamed the Video Game Championships (VGC).

Battles [use the following rules](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Rule_variants "Rule variants") in general:

*   The format is [Double Battles](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Double_Battle "Double Battle"). A player must bring between 4 and 6 Pokémon and select 4 of them just before the battle. In games that use Team Preview ([Generation V](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_V "Generation V") onward), this selection is made after viewing the opponent's 6 Pokémon.
*   Two Pokémon may not have the same Pokédex number. [Special Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Special_Pok%C3%A9mon "Special Pokémon"), [Mythical Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mythical_Pok%C3%A9mon "Mythical Pokémon"), and [Ash-Greninja](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash-Greninja "Ash-Greninja") are disallowed (but not Dusk Form [Lycanroc](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lycanroc_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Lycanroc (Pokémon)")) unless the format has an exception. 
    *   The [Soul Dew](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Soul_Dew "Soul Dew") was disallowed until [Generation VII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VII "Generation VII"), where its effect changed.
    *   [Event](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Event_Pok%C3%A9mon "Event Pokémon")-exclusive [moves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Event_Pok%C3%A9mon#Event-exclusive_moves "Event Pokémon") and [items](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Event_item "Event item") are allowed unless the format explicitly says otherwise.

*   Between [Generation VI](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VI "Generation VI") and [Generation VIII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VIII "Generation VIII"), Pokémon must have an [origin mark](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Origin_mark "Origin mark") matching the games used for the competition. This may be substituted with the [battle-ready symbol](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Battle-ready_symbol "Battle-ready symbol").
*   Two Pokémon may not have the same [held item](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Held_item "Held item").
*   In [Generation IX](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_IX "Generation IX") (including [Pokémon Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "Pokémon Champions")), open team sheets are used. Both players must disclose their team to their opponent, including Tera Type (Pokémon Scarlet/Violet), species, forms, moves, Abilities, held items, and natures (Pokémon Champions), but excluding stats.
*   Pokémon cannot battle above level 50. 
    *   In 2008 and 2009, there was no auto-leveling and Pokémon above level 50 were disallowed outright.
    *   Between 2010 and 2016, Pokémon above level 50 were auto-leveled down to 50, but Pokémon below level 50 were not auto-leveled up.
    *   From 2017 onward, all Pokémon are auto-leveled to 50.

*   Two Pokémon may not have the same nickname. A Pokémon may not be nicknamed the name of a different Pokémon, and nicknames and Trainer names may not be inappropriate.

    *   For this year only, players were only allowed to bring exactly 4 Pokémon, instead of bringing 6 and choosing 4 just before the battle.[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-2)

(It was not possible to obtain Tyranitar at or below level 50 until a [Generation VI](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VI "Generation VI") event.)
    *   The Japan-only (at the time) [Micle Berry](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Micle_Berry "Micle Berry"), [Custap Berry](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Custap_Berry "Custap Berry"), and [Sketching](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sketch_(move) "Sketch (move)")[Seed Flare](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Seed_Flare_(move) "Seed Flare (move)") were disallowed.

Pokémon and regional forms not in the Paldea Pokédex, such as [Quagsire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Quagsire_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Quagsire (Pokémon)") and Johtonian [Wooper](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wooper_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Wooper (Pokémon)"), were disallowed. [Paradox Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paradox_Pok%C3%A9mon "Paradox Pokémon") and the [treasures of ruin](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Treasures_of_ruin "Treasures of ruin") were also disallowed. 
            *   January 2, 2023 was the TPCi start date for Regulation Set A,[[7]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-7) while the TPC start date was instead December 2, 2022.[[8]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-8) The start date of Regulation Set A for [Ranked Battles](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ranked_Battle "Ranked Battle") online was also December 2, 2022.

            *   Prior to the release of [Pokémon HOME](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_HOME "Pokémon HOME") compatibility, the Japanese and Chinese rulesets consistently stated (for all three regulation sets) that a Scarlet and Violet origin mark was required,[[9]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-10) while the English/French/Italian/German/Spanish rulesets consistently stated (for all three regulation sets) that Pokémon transferred from HOME would become allowed when the feature was released.[[11]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-11) (No ruleset was published in Korean due to all Korean Scarlet/Violet tournaments up to that point being conducted online.)
            *   When HOME compatibility was released, the English/French/Italian/German/Spanish ruleset was changed to state that a Scarlet and Violet origin mark was required for the rest of the series (with the only competitive effect being to disallow Roaming Form [Gimmighoul](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gimmighoul "Gimmighoul")).
            *   Regardless of these regional inconsistencies and changes, the HOME update also caused [Plates](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Plate "Plate") and six certain [Egg Moves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Egg_Move "Egg Move") ([Heal Bell](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Heal_Bell_(move) "Heal Bell (move)"), [Simple Beam](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Simple_Beam_(move) "Simple Beam (move)"), [Cosmic Power](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Cosmic_Power_(move) "Cosmic Power (move)"), [Raging Fury](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Raging_Fury_(move) "Raging Fury (move)"), [Barb Barrage](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Barb_Barrage_(move) "Barb Barrage (move)"), and [Psyshield Bash](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psyshield_Bash_(move) "Psyshield Bash (move)")[[12]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-12)) to become newly available and allowed immediately in all regions, at approximately 4pm JST May 30.
            *   Players competing in events in Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, South Korea, and Hong Kong between June 3–4, who were required to lock in their teams by 9am May 31, were sent an email at 11:10pm May 30 stating that the newly available Plates and Egg Moves would be disallowed for those events.[[13]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-13) Players competing in Japan between June 10–11 were sent a similar email on June 1. Events in other locations on the same days were unaffected and Plates/the Egg Moves were allowed.

For example, the Korean League Season 1 on December 15–16, 2019 used 2020 Series 1 rules, while the Kuala Lumpur Regionals on December 21–22, 2019 used 2019 Ultra Series rules.[[17]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-17)

### Broadcasting

*   In 2008, for at least the semifinals onward, players connected their [Nintendo DSes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Nintendo_DS "Nintendo DS") to a modified, unreleased version of [Pokémon Battle Revolution](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Battle_Revolution "Pokémon Battle Revolution"). The modified game featured a unique remix of _Battle! (Team Galactic Boss)_ seemingly arranged for the event, as well as no region- or language-locking.[[18]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-18) No Battle Revolution-specific clauses were set.
*   In 2009, for at least the semifinals onward, players connected their Nintendo DSes to a modified, unreleased version of Pokémon Battle Revolution. The modified game featured Platinum outfits for [Dawn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dawn_(game) "Dawn (game)") and [Lucas](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lucas_(game) "Lucas (game)") as well as no region- or language-locking.[[19]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-19)
*   Between 2010 and 2019, only the top screen of the Nintendo DS or [Nintendo 3DS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Nintendo_3DS "Nintendo 3DS") was broadcast in order to prevent revealing a player's move selections.
*   Between 2023 and 2026, in western, non-World Championships tournaments utilizing [Pokémon Scarlet and Violet](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Scarlet_and_Violet "Pokémon Scarlet and Violet"), one player's screen is directly broadcasted, revealing a player's decisions as they select their move choice. For Asian tournaments, the top 16 matches of the 2023 World Championships and onwards, and the 2024 and 2025 World Championships finals for each division, a third console is connected to the two competitors' consoles in an unreleased LAN spectator mode in order to prevent revealing a player's move selections.
*   From 2026, the spectator mode integrated into private battle rooms in [Pokémon Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "Pokémon Champions") was used to broadcast all matches without revealing either player's move selections.

The **Pokémon World Championships** (Japanese: **ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス**_Pokémon World Championships_), often referred to as simply **Worlds** or abbreviated as **WCS** are an annual event held by the [Play! Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Play!_Pok%C3%A9mon "Play! Pokémon") organized play division of [The Pokémon Company International](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/The_Pok%C3%A9mon_Company_International "The Pokémon Company International"). They function as the finals for both the [Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") and [Video Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Core_series "Core series") Championships. Since 2015, the World Championships have also featured events for [spin-off Pokémon games](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Spin-off_Pok%C3%A9mon_games "Spin-off Pokémon games"), namely [Pokkén Tournament](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pokk%C3%A9n_Tournament "Pokkén Tournament"), [Pokémon GO](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO "Pokémon GO"), and [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE"). The Pokémon World Championships are held annually, occurring every August.

Competitors usually must qualify for the event based on their performance in other events in the same season, such as regional championships, national championships, dedicated qualifying tournaments, or the previous year's World Championships. The exact qualification requirements depend on the year, the region the player is from, and the game in which they are playing.

While the Pokémon World Championships are held as a single unified event featuring multiple different games, each of the games are run as an entirely separate tournament. Competitors compete in only one of the featured games, and the qualification requirements of each are entirely separate. Additionally, competitors usually are separated into one of three age groups, meaning that three world champions are crowned for each game each year.

Minor announcements are usually made during the events, such as upcoming VGC mechanics and variants of TCG cards, teasers for the ruleset of the following VGC format, and the city where the next World Championships will be hosted.

## History

### Predecessors

Before the introduction of the modern Pokémon World Championships, both the TCG and video games held some international competitions.

For the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the [Pokémon Tropical Mega Battle](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Tropical_Mega_Battle "Pokémon Tropical Mega Battle") was an international Pokémon Trading Card Game tournament held annually from 1999 to 2002 in Hawaii by [Wizards of the Coast](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wizards_of_the_Coast "Wizards of the Coast"), the distributor of the Pokémon Trading Card Game in many regions outside of Japan at the time. Players from Canada, Latin America, Europe, the United States, and Japan were invited to the event.

In September 2000, to coincide with the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "wp:2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, Australia, the [first ever Pokémon World Championship](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/w/index.php?title=2000_World_Championships&action=edit&redlink=1 "2000 World Championships (page does not exist)") was also held in Sydney. Players from Australia, Belgium, [France](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_France "Pokémon in France"), [Germany](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_Germany "Pokémon in Germany"), [the Netherlands](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_the_Netherlands "Pokémon in the Netherlands"), [Spain](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_Spain "Pokémon in Spain"), [the United Kingdom](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_the_United_Kingdom "Pokémon in the United Kingdom"), and [the United States](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_in_the_United_States "Pokémon in the United States") competed using [Pokémon Red and Blue](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions") and [Pokémon Yellow](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version "Pokémon Yellow Version"). This was a one-time event, with a video game World Championship not being held again until 2009.

### Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships

In August 2002, Wizards of the Coast held the [first Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championship](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2002_World_Championships_(TCG) "2002 World Championships (TCG)") in Seattle, Washington in the United States.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-1)

Due to Wizards of the Coast's license to distribute the Pokémon Trading Card Game reverting to The Pokémon Company in 2003, no World Championship was held that year. Now with control of the Pokémon Trading Card Game licence, [Pokémon USA](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_USA "Pokémon USA") formed [Pokémon Organized Play](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Organized_Play "Pokémon Organized Play") to manage Pokémon Trading Card Game events.

In August 2004, Pokémon Organized Play held the [2004 Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2004_World_Championships_(TCG) "2004 World Championships (TCG)"). From 2004 to 2008, the event was titled the Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships, reflecting the fact that it was specifically for the Pokémon Trading Card Game only.

At the [2008 Pokémon Trading Card Game World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2008_World_Championships_(TCG) "2008 World Championships (TCG)"), a special video game event called the [Pokémon Video Game Showdown 2008](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Video_Game_Showdown_2008 "Pokémon Video Game Showdown 2008") was held. This event featured players from the United States and Japan competing with [Pokémon Diamond and Pearl](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Diamond_and_Pearl_Versions "Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Versions"). However, since only two countries were involved, the winner was not awarded the title of world champion.

### Pokémon World Championships

In August 2009, the first unified Pokémon World Championships were held, featuring both the Pokémon Trading Card Game and the Pokémon Video Game Championships. This has been the structure used for the Pokémon World Championships ever since.

From 2015 to 2022, [Pokkén Tournament](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pokk%C3%A9n_Tournament "Pokkén Tournament") was also featured at the Pokémon World Championships. In 2015, the Pokkén Tournament competition was run as an invitational due to the lack of preliminary events. After the 2022 World Championships, it was announced that Pokkén Tournament would no longer appear at the Pokémon World Championships.

Starting in 2019, [Pokémon GO](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO "Pokémon GO") was added to the Pokémon World Championships. In 2019, the Pokémon GO competition was run as an invitational due to the lack of preliminary events.

Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the planned 2020 Pokémon World Championships to be held in London, England were cancelled, and the event also was not held in 2021. The World Championships returned with the [2022 Pokémon World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2022_World_Championships "2022 World Championships"), held in London, England like the original 2020 plan.

From 2022 to 2026, [Pokémon UNITE](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE "Pokémon UNITE") was featured the Pokémon World Championships. Beginning with the 2027 competitive season, UNITE's championship tournament will instead be held at a separate event, the [Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_UNITE_Aeos_Crown_2027_Tokyo&action=edit&redlink=1 "Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo (page does not exist)").

## Video Game Championship

The [core series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Core_series "Core series") Pokémon games were first featured at a Nintendo-organized World Championship event in 2000 with single battles, and later returning as [Pokémon Video Game Showdown](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Video_Game_Showdown "Pokémon Video Game Showdown") (VGS) in 2008 as a side-event to the [2008 Trading Card Game World Championships](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2008_World_Championships_(TCG) "2008 World Championships (TCG)") with double battles. Starting in 2009, the events were renamed the Video Game Championships (VGC).

Battles [use the following rules](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Rule_variants "Rule variants") in general:

*   The format is [Double Battles](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Double_Battle "Double Battle"). A player must bring between 4 and 6 Pokémon and select 4 of them just before the battle. In games that use Team Preview ([Generation V](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_V "Generation V") onward), this selection is made after viewing the opponent's 6 Pokémon.
*   Two Pokémon may not have the same Pokédex number. [Special Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Special_Pok%C3%A9mon "Special Pokémon"), [Mythical Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mythical_Pok%C3%A9mon "Mythical Pokémon"), and [Ash-Greninja](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ash-Greninja "Ash-Greninja") are disallowed (but not Dusk Form [Lycanroc](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lycanroc_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Lycanroc (Pokémon)")) unless the format has an exception. 
    *   The [Soul Dew](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Soul_Dew "Soul Dew") was disallowed until [Generation VII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VII "Generation VII"), where its effect changed.
    *   [Event](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Event_Pok%C3%A9mon "Event Pokémon")-exclusive [moves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Event_Pok%C3%A9mon#Event-exclusive_moves "Event Pokémon") and [items](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Event_item "Event item") are allowed unless the format explicitly says otherwise.

*   Between [Generation VI](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VI "Generation VI") and [Generation VIII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VIII "Generation VIII"), Pokémon must have an [origin mark](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Origin_mark "Origin mark") matching the games used for the competition. This may be substituted with the [battle-ready symbol](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Battle-ready_symbol "Battle-ready symbol").
*   Two Pokémon may not have the same [held item](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Held_item "Held item").
*   In [Generation IX](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_IX "Generation IX") (including [Pokémon Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "Pokémon Champions")), open team sheets are used. Both players must disclose their team to their opponent, including Tera Type (Pokémon Scarlet/Violet), species, forms, moves, Abilities, held items, and natures (Pokémon Champions), but excluding stats.
*   Pokémon cannot battle above level 50. 
    *   In 2008 and 2009, there was no auto-leveling and Pokémon above level 50 were disallowed outright.
    *   Between 2010 and 2016, Pokémon above level 50 were auto-leveled down to 50, but Pokémon below level 50 were not auto-leveled up.
    *   From 2017 onward, all Pokémon are auto-leveled to 50.

*   Two Pokémon may not have the same nickname. A Pokémon may not be nicknamed the name of a different Pokémon, and nicknames and Trainer names may not be inappropriate.

        *   [Regulation Set G](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_G "Regulation Set G") (May 1 - Aug 31, 2024): Up to one Special Pokémon is allowed.

*   **[2025](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2025_Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships "2025 Pokémon World Championships")** — [Pokémon Scarlet and Violet](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Scarlet_and_Violet "Pokémon Scarlet and Violet")
    *   The season was split into the following series: 
        *   [Regulation Set H](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_H "Regulation Set H") (Sep 1, 2024 - Jan 5, 2025): Legendary and Paradox Pokémon became disallowed.
        *   [Regulation Set G](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_G "Regulation Set G") (rerun) (Jan 6 - Apr 30, 2025): Legendary Pokémon, Paradox Pokémon, and up to one Special Pokémon became re-allowed.
        *   [Regulation Set I](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_I "Regulation Set I") (May 1 - Aug 31, 2025): Up to two Special Pokémon are allowed.

*   **[2026](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2026_Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships "2026 Pokémon World Championships")** — [Pokémon Scarlet and Violet](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Scarlet_and_Violet "Pokémon Scarlet and Violet") → [Pokémon Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "Pokémon Champions")
    *   The season was split into the following series: 
        *   Regulation Set H (rerun) (Sep 1 - Nov 30, 2025): Legendary and Paradox Pokémon became disallowed. 
            *   [Ranked Battles](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ranked_Battle "Ranked Battle") online instead used Regulation Set J, where up to two Special Pokémon (including Mythical Pokémon) are allowed.

        *   Regulation Set F (rerun) (Dec 1, 2025 - March 31, 2026): Legendary and Paradox Pokémon became re-allowed, but no Special Pokémon were allowed. 
            *   Ranked Battles online instead shifted from Regulation Set J to a rerun of Regulation Set I on January 5, 2026.

        *   Regulation Set I (rerun) (April 1, 2026 - May 31, 2026[[16]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-16)): Up to two Special Pokémon are allowed.
        *   [Regulation Set M-A](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_M-A "Regulation Set M-A") (April 8 - June 17, 2026): The 186 Pokémon species and 59 Mega Evolutions [currently obtainable in Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_in_Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "List of Pokémon in Pokémon Champions") are allowed, including transfer-only Pokémon and Mega Stones.
        *   [Regulation Set M-B](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_M-B "Regulation Set M-B") (June 17 - September 9, 2026): A further 22 species and 15 Mega Evolutions were allowed into Champions.

*   [**2027**](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/2027_Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships "2027 Pokémon World Championships") — [Pokémon Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "Pokémon Champions")
    *   The season was split into the following series: 
        *   [Regulation Set M-C](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Regulation_Set_M-C "Regulation Set M-C") (September 9 - December 2, 2026): Another 23 species and 6 Mega Evolutions were allowed into Champions, including 3 Z-Mega Evolutions.

When series may overlap at the start of a new game release, events may use either of the two formats. For example, the Korean League Season 1 on December 15–16, 2019 used 2020 Series 1 rules, while the Kuala Lumpur Regionals on December 21–22, 2019 used 2019 Ultra Series rules.[[17]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-17)

### Broadcasting

*   In 2008, for at least the semifinals onward, players connected their [Nintendo DSes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Nintendo_DS "Nintendo DS") to a modified, unreleased version of [Pokémon Battle Revolution](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Battle_Revolution "Pokémon Battle Revolution"). The modified game featured a unique remix of _Battle! (Team Galactic Boss)_ seemingly arranged for the event, as well as no region- or language-locking.[[18]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-18) No Battle Revolution-specific clauses were set.
*   In 2009, for at least the semifinals onward, players connected their Nintendo DSes to a modified, unreleased version of Pokémon Battle Revolution. The modified game featured Platinum outfits for [Dawn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dawn_(game) "Dawn (game)") and [Lucas](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Lucas_(game) "Lucas (game)") as well as no region- or language-locking.[[19]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Video_Game_Championships#cite_note-19)
*   Between 2010 and 2019, only the top screen of the Nintendo DS or [Nintendo 3DS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Nintendo_3DS "Nintendo 3DS") was broadcast in order to prevent revealing a player's move selections.
*   Between 2023 and 2026, in western, non-World Championships tournaments utilizing [Pokémon Scarlet and Violet](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Scarlet_and_Violet "Pokémon Scarlet and Violet"), one player's screen is directly broadcasted, revealing a player's decisions as they select their move choice. For Asian tournaments, the top 16 matches of the 2023 World Championships and onwards, and the 2024 and 2025 World Championships finals for each division, a third console is connected to the two competitors' consoles in an unreleased LAN spectator mode in order to prevent revealing a player's move selections.
*   From 2026, the spectator mode integrated into private battle rooms in [Pokémon Champions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champions "Pokémon Champions") was used to broadcast all matches without revealing either player's move selections.
